newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliament rejects draft law on Iraq ties.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament rejects draft law on Iraq ties.

text.p: Russia's upper chamber of parliament on Friday rejected a draft law seeking a renewal of trade between Russia and Iraq and calling on the Kremlin to ignore international sanctions against Baghdad.
The Federation Council voted 68 to 37 to reject the draft bill, passed by the State Duma lower chamber one month ago and proposed by ultra-nationalists headed by Vladimir Zhirinovsky.
The Council's international affairs commitee said the law violated the constitution which gives the president overall charge of foreign policy.
The bill would re-establish trade ties, allow Russia to buy Iraqi oil, export machinery and render humanitarian aid.

Baghdad owes Moscow billions of dollars in Soviet-era debts and Russian officials have argued for lifting stringent oil sanctions against Iraq, imposed by the United Nations after Iraqi troops invaded neighbouring Kuwait in 1990.

Under a deal with the U.N., Iraq was allowed from December to June to export $2 billion worth of oil to raise money for urgent needs and Russian firms fought hard to get the oil purchase contracts late last year.
The deal was renewed by the U.N. Security Council for another six months from June 8, but Baghdad cannot start oil exports until the U.N. approves an aid distribution plan drawn up by Baghdad.
The Federation Council also rejected a draft law aimed at boosting cooperation with Lybia.
